analysis:
Reviewed all four primary analyses and all supplied replayed patches/metadata. The changes concern CI source, dependency and build-cache custody, relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-034/T-054; they do not directly change TB-002/TB-011 authorization, attestation verification, plaintext handling, encryption, billing or runtime prefix-cache isolation (T-041).

The provider-ci-build patch independently confirms default-off cache writes (.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml:7-9), caller opt-in on build/SwiftPM/Metal saves (107,116,143), and new SwiftPM repository restoration partitioned by OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles (47-53). These controls narrow existing writes. Broad fallback restoration alone does not establish an adversarial writer into a trusted cache scope. docs-impact.yml:61-68 adds blobless history and sparse exclusions without changing the selected PR revision or validation commands. The changelog and build documentation describe daily Git caches, credential removal and cold-checkout fallback, but documentation is not proof of implementation.

No independently supported regression qualifies for a finding. Integration replay omits 13 reviewed source units, including executable ci.yml checkout/save sequences. Consequently, prior questions about every SAVE_CACHES caller, token-free Git metadata, checkout revision/submodule correctness, full-history provenance behavior and routed-runner cache producer trust cannot be fully resolved from the replay. These are unverified contracts, not demonstrated bypasses. A further pass should inspect those ci.yml sequences alongside the composite action and verify sparse exclusions against the affected validation inputs. No supplied evidence establishes release consumption of these cache families or a new qualification/serving claim.
